1. An exact transformation of the nonunital normalization problem

The strongest new representation obtained here separates the adjoint dynamics into a genuine native CPTP evolution and a weak local Hermitian potential. It works for the supplied general multiqubit GKLS perturbations and preserves their complete schedule descriptions.

Write one local generator as

 $\mathcal D(X)
=-i[K,X]
+\sum_\alpha r_\alpha
\left(
V_\alpha XV_\alpha^\dagger
-\frac12\{V_\alpha^\dagger V_\alpha,X\}
\right).$ Define

 $A_{\mathcal D}:=\mathcal D(I)
=\sum_\alpha r_\alpha
\left(V_\alpha V_\alpha^\dagger-V_\alpha^\dagger V_\alpha\right)$ and

 $\mathcal G_{\mathcal D}(X)
=+i[K,X]
+\sum_\alpha r_\alpha
\left(
V_\alpha^\dagger XV_\alpha
-\frac12\{V_\alpha V_\alpha^\dagger,X\}
\right).$ The latter is a trace-preserving GKLS generator, with Hamiltonian  $-K$  and jumps  $V_\alpha^\dagger$ . Direct substitution gives

 $\boxed{
\mathcal D^*(X)
=\mathcal G_{\mathcal D}(X)
+\frac12\{A_{\mathcal D},X\}.
}
\tag{1}$ For a term on at most  $k$  qubits, the supplied diamond-norm promise implies the conservative bounds

 $\|A_{\mathcal D}\|_\infty\le 2^k,
\qquad
\|\mathcal G_{\mathcal D}\|_\diamond
\le c_k:=4^k+2^k.
\tag{2}$ Thus  $\mathcal G_{\mathcal D}/c_k$  fits the original normalized local-generator class, with perturbation coefficient  $c_k\eta_z$ . Applying the accepted predictor to this CPTP part requires its threshold at that rescaled coefficient.
